summary:
Status: the csharp fix round is done. Every one of the reviewer's 8 required fixes has an outcome, and `ok` is false only because the one command still fails on recorded `defect` classes that wait for shared changes.

What changed:
- Three fixes in csharp's own files:
  - The accessor citation in hand record dae78da098 now names MainEntity_csharp.ts:25-28 (the file is 36 lines).
  - The body.once citation now quotes the code that reads a Stream in full (Media.cs:116-120) instead of a comment.
  - The MarkDeleted and Deleted reasons now say what the pipeline does: it marks the entity on any successful op named remove, Stream("remove", ...) included (EntityBase.fragment.cs:233-240, 281, 306).
- Four fixes need shared changes, recorded below and not made: root quick start naming (CS0136), the stream-signal sentence, callcheck, and the guard's citation check.
  - The stream sentence prints `callopts.signal`, which C# cannot write; the key is `callopts["signal"]` and only a CancellationToken counts. I recorded its class 80f77307dc (x94) as a `defect`. The reviewer called it awkward rather than false. I recorded it anyway, because the provider cannot respell a shared sentence.
  - The 3 rootquick defect classes stay as the porter recorded them.
- The eighth fix (declare a new fact and remove the three defect records) waits on the naming change.

Final numbers, after a build that exits 0 and leaves `git status` empty:
- Guard 4/4, guard plus reader 81/81.
- Suite 2,630 of 2,635 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. Golden 2/2, unchanged.
- The reviewed one command with REGEN=1 exits 1. Its only failing numbers are reference ledger defect 1 and rootquick blocks defect 3.
- The SCRATCH=1 numbers equal the porter's.
- The pages are byte-identical to the ones the reviewer read, and no other language's page changed.

No C# compiler is here (dotnet, csc and mono are all missing), so the 30 changed blocks are still compiled by nothing. The single csharp lane that reports a pass returns early without dotnet, so it ran nothing.

outcomes.finding: 3. Hand record dae78da098 cites MainEntity_csharp.ts:172-175, which does not exist
outcomes.how: The reviewer is right: MainEntity_csharp.ts is 36 lines, and the accessor `public ${model.const.Name}EntityBase ${entity.Name}(...)` / `return new global::${model.const.Name}Sdk.Entity.${cls}(this, entopts);` is at :25-28. The reason now cites :25-28. A grep over the provider, hook, forms and hand file found no other copy of the wrong lines. The porter's report text (accessor.sig, accessor.cached) should read :25-28 too. After the fix: hand records 233, STALE 0.

outcomes.finding: 4. Forms citation ref.facts.body.once leans on a comment ('// Bytes, a Stream or a string, sent as they are. A Stream can be read')
outcomes.how: Media.cs:110-112 is a comment; :116-120 is the code that reads the stream in full. The quote is now ['if (body is Stream stream)', 'stream.CopyTo(buffer);', 'return buffer.ToArray();'] (each occurs once in Media.cs). The guard account report shows the citation quoting code only; the guard passes 4/4 and guard plus reader 81/81. The account line is unchanged: derived 47, cited 17, language 1, convention 6.

outcomes.finding: 5. Forms undocumented.MarkDeleted reason 'set by Remove itself' is not what the runtime does
outcomes.how: The reviewer is right. Stream builds its context with `["opname"] = action` (EntityBase.fragment.cs:281) and runs `RunOp` (:306). RunPipeline then calls MarkDeleted whenever `ctx.Result.Ok` and opname is "remove" (:233-240), and MarkDeleted is public (:28). The reason now says this. The sibling reason for Deleted ('whether Remove succeeded on this instance') had the same fault and is reworded too. No page fact rests on either reason; the pages are byte-identical before and after.

outcomes.finding: 6. ReadmeRef.ts STREAM_SIGNAL prints the literal `callopts.signal` and does not say a C# signal must be a CancellationToken
outcomes.how: Checked: EntityBase.fragment.cs:267-270 reads `StructUtils.GetProp(callopts, "signal") is CancellationToken sigTok ? sigTok : CancellationToken.None`. callopts is a Dictionary<string, object?>?, so the C# spelling is `callopts["signal"]`, and any value other than a CancellationToken is ignored. The sentence is one literal (ts/src/cmp/ReadmeRef.ts:123, used at :119), and the provider may not respell it. Class 80f77307dc (reference, x94 in 18 variations), until now matched automatically as shared:ts, is recorded as `defect` in hand/csharp.json naming ReadmeRef.ts. The reason of token class eea38408c0 now names the C# key. The reviewer judged it awkward, not false; I record it as a defect because the code span is not C# and the guide's rule is that a page shared code cannot make right is a defect.

outcomes.finding: 7. tools/callcheck.js silently drops printed calls to undeclared members (MEMBER 0) and misses an instance accessor called on the type (RECEIVER 0)
outcomes.how: It is a shared tools file, so I did not touch it. No csharp page carries such a call: callcheck checks 386 calls of 20 runtime members with 0 findings, and the reviewer's misses (`.Lode(`, `DemoSDK.Planet().Load(`, `.Fetch(`, `.Record()`) were injected edits. So there is no class to mark `defect`. Recorded under shared_changes_needed.

outcomes.finding: 8. Guard citation check compares a cited code value with its quote as a set of tokens (B1/B3 passed)
outcomes.how: It is a shared guard file (ts/test/runtimeforms/account.ts checkCitation, :299-306, codeTokens :113), so I did not touch it. No csharp page fact is wrong. Read: container `Dictionary<string, object?>` stands contiguous in 'public ProjectNameSDK(Dictionary<string, object?>? options = null)'; none `null` in 'entopts = null'; okFalse `false` in '["ok"] = false,'; ctor[0] 'using {module};' in order in 'using ProjectNameSdk.Feature;'. So there is no class to mark `defect`. Recorded under shared_changes_needed.

shared_changes_needed.file: ts/src/helpers/example.ts (refOf :219-227, RuntimeFacts type) and ts/src/cmp/ReadmeQuick.ts (topQuickText :246, bare :236-239)
shared_changes_needed.change: An optional RuntimeFacts flag, e.g. `blockScope?: true` (a local is in scope over its whole block). Where it is set and VarNaming is 'entity', refOf names role 'item' by the generic item name through the hook's layout.vars (`vars.item ?? 'item'`, as GENERIC does), whenever the same section also binds role 'one' or 'created' for that entity. The reviewer's alternative is a language-neutral rule (always name the item apart when one section binds both roles of one entity), but that changes the root quick start of every ported language.
shared_changes_needed.why: bare() puts `foreach (var planet in planets)` and `var planet = ...` in one C# block. That is CS0136, and it breaks 5 of 21 root quick starts (crud-bare, crud-basic, crud-noupdate, doc-crud, ex-readonly); OLD used planetItem and compiled. Read, not compiled.
shared_changes_needed.providers_forced: The flag: csharp only (declare it, then remove defect records 8c5a4fbe41, 3d4aae6c8d, b2b5fd8804). Read, not compiled: java, kotlin, scala, cpp, js and php accept a later outer declaration after a loop variable. The language-neutral alternative would be breaking by the guide's definition (changed root blocks in all thirteen ported languages, each to be re-reviewed), though no provider code would change.

shared_changes_needed.file: ts/src/cmp/ReadmeRef.ts (STREAM_SIGNAL :122-123, used in streamText :119) and ts/src/helpers/example.ts (RefSyntax.key :473)
shared_changes_needed.change: Print the key through the provider: 'It ends early once ' + code(r.key('callopts', ['signal'])) + ' reports an abort.', and widen key's container union from 'options' | 'fetchargs' to include 'callopts'. Add an optional cited fact (for example ref.facts.streamSignalType) naming the only value the stream honours, printed in the same sentence.
shared_changes_needed.why: csharp prints `callopts.signal`, which is not C#: its key is `callopts["signal"]`, and only a CancellationToken ends the stream (EntityBase.fragment.cs:267-270). Class 80f77307dc (x94) is recorded as `defect` until then.
shared_changes_needed.providers_forced: Breaking by the guide's definition: a changed sentence. The code span changes in csharp, go, py, rb, swift and perl (their key printers write `callopts["signal"]` / `$callopts->{signal}`); ts prints the same, and lua through its own index printer. clojure, elixir and ocaml must change their key printer: it prints the path alone (Syntax_clojure.ts:214, Syntax_elixir.ts:171, Syntax_ocaml.ts:226), so the sentence would read `signal`. The type fact is additive, declared by csharp (CancellationToken), and when ported by java (BooleanSupplier, EntityBase.fragment.java:214-216), kotlin (Function0, EntityBase.fragment.kt:233-235) and scala (EntityBase.fragment.scala:210, not read in full). Every language with streamSignal re-reviews the sentence class.

shared_changes_needed.change: Report a printed call to a member the runtime does not declare as MEMBER, instead of dropping it from the count. Report an instance accessor called on the client type (DemoSDK.Planet()) as RECEIVER.
shared_changes_needed.why: Reviewer's runs: `.Fetch(`, `.Record()` and `.Lode(` lowered the call count (386 to 326, 342 and 385) with MEMBER 0, and `DemoSDK.Planet().Load(` gave RECEIVER 0.
shared_changes_needed.providers_forced: none (a tools check). A port whose pages print such a call would newly fail; csharp's pages print none (0 findings over 386 calls).

shared_changes_needed.change: For a code-valued cited fact, compare the value with the quote as a sequence: its tokens in order, adjacent after whitespace normalisation and slot removal. Not as a set of tokens each found anywhere in the quote.
shared_changes_needed.why: Reviewer's runs: container 'Dictionary<string, object>' and 'Dictionary<object?, string>' both passed, because every token stands in 'public ProjectNameSDK(Dictionary<string, object?>? options = null)'.
shared_changes_needed.providers_forced: No interface change. Forms work only in a language whose code-valued citation quotes its tokens out of order. csharp's container, none, okFalse and ctor[0] hold in order (read).
